questions.text: Which flags does this add, what type is each (release, ops, experiment, permission), what is its default, and when is it removed? Without anyone setting a variable, what does a user see after the merge?
Which env keys are new or changed, and are they declared in the schema and present (by name) in every target environment?
In what order must secrets, migrations, schedules and code land, and does each step survive if the next one fails?
Which external clients or protocols consume this, and how is each one tested?
Which host, route or redirect config does this touch, and what is the URL table to probe after the deploy?
What does this retire, and where is the removal manifest (routes, components, keys, env vars, cron entries, permission keys)?
Does any credential, token, schedule or destination get shared between stage and production?
Does any step read a shared mutable directory or a fail-open loader?
Pre-mortem: it is a week later and this release failed. What is the most likely reason?

budgets.measure: env names per target vs the schema's required keys (names only)

rules.title: Feature gated by process.env.X === 'true' (off when the variable is absent)
rules.why: A finished feature ships invisible until someone sets a variable in every environment.
rules.confirm: failing-test: boot with no flag variables; the feature's smoke test fails
rules.fixHint: release and ops toggles default ON with OFF as the lever, read through the config schema

rules.title: process.env.X || '' / ?? '' / non-null assertion (silent empty config)
rules.why: A missing key becomes an empty string that fails later, far from the cause.
rules.confirm: failing-test: boot with an empty env; the process starts instead of exiting with the key's name
rules.fixHint: one schema reads process.env and fails fast at startup

rules.title: dotenvx run without --strict (fails open: missing file injects nothing)
rules.why: A typo in the env path runs the command with zero variables and exit 0.
rules.confirm: repro-script: point -f at a missing file; the command still runs
rules.fixHint: add --strict, then probe the loaded key names

rules.title: Tunnel host committed (ngrok, trycloudflare, loca.lt)
rules.why: A dead or someone else's tunnel becomes a production callback URL.
rules.confirm: static-proof: the host is in a committed value
rules.fixHint: per-environment host from config, validated against an allowlist

rules.title: New required key or migration with no 'how to deploy' order in the PR
rules.why: Code lands before its key and crash-loops.
rules.confirm: failing-test: boot the new build with the old env; it crashes instead of degrading

rules.title: Schedule, cron or webhook created by hand, not declared in the repo
rules.why: Undeclared infrastructure drifts and points at the wrong host.
rules.confirm: measurement: live schedule list vs the declared list differs

rules.title: Retired flag name reused for a new meaning, or a deleted page whose route/keys/cron remain
rules.confirm: repro-script: git log -S<flag> shows the old meaning; retired URL returns 200

rules.title: 'Tested in client A' generalized to every client
rules.why: Each client discovers and authenticates differently.
rules.confirm: measurement: client matrix run records a failure

rules.title: Generated code or build cache shared with other checkouts or sessions (a link or an absolute path outside the worktree)
rules.why: Another session's regenerate empties it and this checkout's running server starts failing.
rules.confirm: repro-script: regenerate in a second checkout; the first checkout's running server starts failing

verify.text: schema-only env access, flag inventory with defaults, --strict on loaders, tunnel-host scan, removal-manifest grep = 0
boot with an empty env -> clear exit or degraded mode; flag absent -> intended default
env names per target vs the schema; schedules vs the declaration; credential hashes differ per environment
follow the written runbook (READ-DO); canary where available
post-deploy probes on stage: health and key presence, host/route table, retired URLs, protocol discovery, smoke test with no flags set, client matrix
